newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 11.

text.p: Three Amada group companies are expected to boost pre-tax profits by more than ten percent this business year to March 1997, helped by increases in orders of machine tools. Amada Co Ltd will return to an operating profit due to wholesale price cuts by group firms.

Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd is expected to post record consolidated net profit of 28 billion yen for the second consecutive year in the business year to March 1997, up 16 percent from a year earlier.

Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd is expected to post 92 billion yen in pre-tax profit in the business year to March 1997, about the same level as last year, and about three billion yen less than a projected forecast, hit by a drop in revenues from asset management due to low interest rates.

Nichirei Corp plans to start growing organic crops to make frozen food in early 1997 in Washington State, in cooperation with Washington-based food processing company Columbia Foods Inc. The company plans to raise its sales of frozen organic products from less than 2,000 tonnes in the year which ended on March 31 to 10,000 tonnes in two years. The move will give Nichirei one of the largest supply capacities among Japanese organic food producers.
